sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible degree route: accredited US bachelor's completed before entry; university GPA guideline 2.75.
Department expects advanced calculus and linear algebra, recommends real analysis, differential equations
and abstract algebra. International students are explicitly welcome; no master's prerequisite. [s1] [s3] [s33]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply in Slate to Mathematics (Ph.D.); optionally specify mathematical subfields. Arrange required Math GRE,
records and referees; assemble the main essay, resume, community essay and suggested course supplement.
No prior supervisor agreement is listed. [s1] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Faculty contacts below are current direct matches; no advance adviser sponsorship requirement found.
Graduate Program Manager Jacob Lagerstrom handles application logistics. Five College colleagues may enrich
seminars but are not automatically UMass primary advisers. [s1] [s2] [s12] [s13] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate receives documents and tracks the checklist. Department does not accept applicant materials directly; do
not send them to faculty as a substitute. No application or referee invitation has been initiated. [s1] [s5]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Math GRE requirement explicitly Fall 2027. January 10deadline is standing on the same current instructions;
university assistantship minimum explicitly September 2026,2027offer unknown. [s1] [s7]

English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: TOEFL new scale 4/old80, IELTS Academic6.5, DET115 or PTE53; two-year validity through entry.
Official agency transmission required. No superscoring/MyBest/IELTS One Skill Retake; no TOEFL Essentials/ITP

two academic years completed before expected entry. John should qualify through recent UChicago study if

teaching screening. [s2] [s4]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Current university minimum effective September 6, 2026 is US$31,342.40 for a nine-month20-hour/week
assistantship ($41.24/hour); not a dated 2027 mathematics offer. Department's fall 2023$25,247 figure is
historical. Eligible appointments provide tuition credit,100%service-fee reduction,95%individual/dependent
health premiums,and free dental/vision; other fees may remain. Summer is additional and not assured. [s6] [s7]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Department says all admitted PhD students are offered funding. TA renewal normally extends five years for
PhD students with satisfactory teaching and progress. An older central description gives four years after a prior
master's, five without; John is in the bachelor's-entry category. Not an unconditional guarantee. [s6] [s8] [s11]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants may receive university funding and departmental TA support; no citizenship exclusion
appears for ordinary admission funding. TA language screening and appointment eligibility still apply. [s2] [s4]
[s6]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Renewal requires satisfactory teaching and academic progress. Current handbook specifies
advanced-calculus/linear-algebra qualification by year2, two more written exams by January of year2, and oral
examination in year3; adviser/dissertation progress thereafter. Older central Basic/Advanced exam
terminology is stale; follow the current handbook and offer. [s8] [s9] [s11]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No additional incoming TA form: admission application is the funding application. Continuing students request
TA renewal and summer appointments separately. [s6] [s8] [s10]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Faculty-grant RAs, limited summer teaching, and departmental summer RAs. Departmental summer RA
requires a declared dissertation adviser, is generally available at most once, and normally excludes prior
faculty-grant RA recipients. Department explicitly cannot fund all interested students over summer. External
fellowships are competitive and award-specific. [s10]
Application fee [Standing rule]
US$90 nonrefundable, paid online when submitting. [s3]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Published routes include McNair documentation or a GRE fee-reduction certificate issued within the previous
year, emailed as PDF to gradfee@grad.umass.edu; GRE-based waiver covers one application. Internal
UMass/Five College routes do not apply to UChicago. No international hardship sponsorship confirmed; ask
before payment. [s3]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible degree route: accredited US bachelor's completed before entry; university GPA guideline 2.75.
Department expects advanced calculus and linear algebra, recommends real analysis, differential equations
and abstract algebra. International students are explicitly welcome; no master's prerequisite. [s1] [s3] [s33]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply in Slate to Mathematics (Ph.D.); optionally specify mathematical subfields. Arrange required Math GRE,
records and referees; assemble the main essay, resume, community essay and suggested course supplement.
No prior supervisor agreement is listed. [s1] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Faculty contacts below are current direct matches; no advance adviser sponsorship requirement found.
Graduate Program Manager Jacob Lagerstrom handles application logistics. Five College colleagues may enrich
seminars but are not automatically UMass primary advisers. [s1] [s2] [s12] [s13] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate receives documents and tracks the checklist. Department does not accept applicant materials directly; do
not send them to faculty as a substitute. No application or referee invitation has been initiated. [s1] [s5]

Math GRE requirement explicitly Fall 2027. January 10deadline is standing on the same current instructions;
university assistantship minimum explicitly September 2026,2027offer unknown. [s1] [s7]

policy but the deadline line itself omits a year; treat January 10 as the standing rule and confirm the portal's
2027 date. February 1 on an older appointment page is superseded. [s1] [s2] [s11]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Admission application also requests support automatically; no separate TA application or earlier funding
deadline. Use the Mathematics January 10 deadline. [s2] [s6]

Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Current university minimum effective September 6, 2026 is US$31,342.40 for a nine-month20-hour/week

health premiums,and free dental/vision; other fees may remain. Summer is additional and not assured. [s6] [s7]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Department says all admitted PhD students are offered funding. TA renewal normally extends five years for
PhD students with satisfactory teaching and progress. An older central description gives four years after a prior
master's, five without; John is in the bachelor's-entry category. Not an unconditional guarantee. [s6] [s8] [s11]

International applicants may receive university funding and departmental TA support; no citizenship exclusion
appears for ordinary admission funding. TA language screening and appointment eligibility still apply. [s2] [s4]

advanced-calculus/linear-algebra qualification by year2, two more written exams by January of year2, and oral

terminology is stale; follow the current handbook and offer. [s8] [s9] [s11]

No additional incoming TA form: admission application is the funding application. Continuing students request
TA renewal and summer appointments separately. [s6] [s8] [s10]

Faculty-grant RAs, limited summer teaching, and departmental summer RAs. Departmental summer RA
requires a declared dissertation adviser, is generally available at most once, and normally excludes prior
faculty-grant RA recipients. Department explicitly cannot fund all interested students over summer. External
fellowships are competitive and award-specific. [s10]

US$90 nonrefundable, paid online when submitting. [s3]

Published routes include McNair documentation or a GRE fee-reduction certificate issued within the previous

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible degree route: accredited US bachelor's completed before entry; university GPA guideline 2.75.
Department expects advanced calculus and linear algebra, recommends real analysis, differential equations
and abstract algebra. International students are explicitly welcome; no master's prerequisite. [s1] [s3] [s33]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply in Slate to Mathematics (Ph.D.); optionally specify mathematical subfields. Arrange required Math GRE,
records and referees; assemble the main essay, resume, community essay and suggested course supplement.
No prior supervisor agreement is listed. [s1] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Faculty contacts below are current direct matches; no advance adviser sponsorship requirement found.
Graduate Program Manager Jacob Lagerstrom handles application logistics. Five College colleagues may enrich
seminars but are not automatically UMass primary advisers. [s1] [s2] [s12] [s13] [s14]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate receives documents and tracks the checklist. Department does not accept applicant materials directly; do
not send them to faculty as a substitute. No application or referee invitation has been initiated. [s1] [s5]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Math GRE requirement explicitly Fall 2027. January 10deadline is standing on the same current instructions;
university assistantship minimum explicitly September 2026,2027offer unknown. [s1] [s7]

Academic application [Conflict]
January 10, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, for fall Mathematics PhD. The page expressly addresses Fall 2027 GRE
policy but the deadline line itself omits a year; treat January 10 as the standing rule and confirm the portal's
2027 date. February 1 on an older appointment page is superseded. [s1] [s2] [s11]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Admission application also requests support automatically; no separate TA application or earlier funding
deadline. Use the Mathematics January 10 deadline. [s2] [s6]

Reference receipt [Unresolved]
No independently dated letter deadline/grace found. Plan receipt by January 10. FAQ says files can reach
review with two letters and omissions explained, but the program requirement remains at least three; this is
not a promised extension for the third letter. [s1] [s2]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
Official GRE/English results sent by agencies, ETS institution 3917. No distinct late-score cutoff or guaranteed
grace identified; arrange arrival by the application deadline. English scores must be valid at intended entry, not
only when applying. [s1] [s4]
Supporting documents [Unresolved]
Submit application materials through Graduate School Slate by the application deadline. Official final records
follow admission; no dated 2027 final-record cutoff located. Incomplete-file review described in FAQ does not
establish an extension. [s1] [s2] [s5]

Department FAQ explicitly describes April 15 as the offer-response deadline (standing, not dated 2027).
Central page also protects time to consider funding until April 15, but contains outdated written-release
language; verify current CGS/offer rules and any interim check-ins. [s2] [s5]

English requirement [Standing rule]
If not exempt: TOEFL new scale 4/old80, IELTS Academic6.5, DET115 or PTE53; two-year validity through entry.
Official agency transmission required. No superscoring/MyBest/IELTS One Skill Retake; no TOEFL Essentials/ITP
Plus or IELTS Indicator. Department expects strong spoken English and may require ITA screening for teaching.
[s2] [s4]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Published exemption routes include an earned US bachelor's/master's, or current full-time US enrollment with
two academic years completed before expected entry. John should qualify through recent UChicago study if
these facts hold; confirm waiver processing in Slate. Admission exemption does not establish exemption from
teaching screening. [s2] [s4]

Strongly recommended, not required. [s1]

Required explicitly for Mathematics PhD Fall 2027; exceptions applying to Statistics or MS programs do not
apply. [s1] [s2]

Central instructions accept unofficial application transcripts from institutions with ≥9 credits, followed by
official records upon admission. Department checklist says all institutions/official transcripts; FAQ says ≥6
credits but acknowledges initial unofficial records. Upload all relevant records and clarify 6-8-credit institutions;
use official transcripts after admission. Non-English records need official translation. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s5]

Suggested useful supplement: mathematics courses with textbooks and instructors. Not described as
mandatory; no template/length limit published. [s1]

descriptions are not specified. Verify optional attachment location rather than assuming extra files are

At least three; central two-letter minimum is insufficient to meet the mathematics program's stated
requirement. Maximum not published. [s1] [s2]

Required personal statement: faithful paraphrase - explain motivation for graduate study in mathematics.
Enter text or upload PDF. No mathematics-specific word/page limit or font requirement found. [s1] [s3]

Separate central short essay, maximum 600 words. Faithful paraphrase: choose a meaningful
community/group, explain its significance and how that experience will enrich both campus/program and
discipline. Exact full prompt is linked. Portal format beyond word limit unverified. [s3]

Suggested supplementary course list with instructor and textbook information; no public page limit, formatting

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Current university minimum effective September 6, 2026 is US$31,342.40 for a nine-month20-hour/week
assistantship ($41.24/hour); not a dated 2027 mathematics offer. Department's fall 2023$25,247 figure is
historical. Eligible appointments provide tuition credit,100%service-fee reduction,95%individual/dependent
health premiums,and free dental/vision; other fees may remain. Summer is additional and not assured. [s6] [s7]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Department says all admitted PhD students are offered funding. TA renewal normally extends five years for
PhD students with satisfactory teaching and progress. An older central description gives four years after a prior
master's, five without; John is in the bachelor's-entry category. Not an unconditional guarantee. [s6] [s8] [s11]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International applicants may receive university funding and departmental TA support; no citizenship exclusion
appears for ordinary admission funding. TA language screening and appointment eligibility still apply. [s2] [s4]
[s6]
Conditions and duties [Conflict]
Renewal requires satisfactory teaching and academic progress. Current handbook specifies
advanced-calculus/linear-algebra qualification by year2, two more written exams by January of year2, and oral
examination in year3; adviser/dissertation progress thereafter. Older central Basic/Advanced exam
terminology is stale; follow the current handbook and offer. [s8] [s9] [s11]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No additional incoming TA form: admission application is the funding application. Continuing students request
TA renewal and summer appointments separately. [s6] [s8] [s10]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Faculty-grant RAs, limited summer teaching, and departmental summer RAs. Departmental summer RA
requires a declared dissertation adviser, is generally available at most once, and normally excludes prior
faculty-grant RA recipients. Department explicitly cannot fund all interested students over summer. External
fellowships are competitive and award-specific. [s10]
Application fee [Standing rule]
US$90 nonrefundable, paid online when submitting. [s3]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Published routes include McNair documentation or a GRE fee-reduction certificate issued within the previous
year, emailed as PDF to gradfee@grad.umass.edu; GRE-based waiver covers one application. Internal
UMass/Five College routes do not apply to UChicago. No international hardship sponsorship confirmed; ask
before payment. [s3]
